entries.proposition: System: five-month-old male mice with a brain-specific glycogen synthase knockout (GYS1 Nestin-KO) versus littermate controls; hippocampal CA1 recordings in awake mice. No WWOX.
entries.snippet: Five-month-old male mice were used for these experiments.

entries.proposition: Hypoxia is hypobaric, 405 mmHg (about 5000 m simulated altitude) for 60 minutes, not a therapeutic oxygen exposure.
entries.snippet: Animals were maintained at this altitude for a total of 60 min
entries.anchor: Methods, Experiments Performed in the Hypobaric Chamber

entries.proposition: Spectral result: in the 6-10 Hz band the knockout power exceeds control under hypobaric exposure (8.6 and 9.2 against 6.8 and 7.0), after no change within either group.
entries.snippet: the spectral power of LFPs in GYS1Nestin-KO were significantly (P ≤ 0.05) larger than those recorded in the WT group, during the 15 and 60 min hypobaric conditions

entries.proposition: Synaptic result at baseline: the knockout CA3-CA1 synapse is already more excitable at ground level; hypoxia raises control excitability but the knockout differences vanish at 60 minutes and return 24 hours later.
entries.snippet: differences were abolished during the hypoxic episode, and recovered

entries.proposition: The same paragraph's earlier sentence and the Figure 2 legend say recovery was seen at 24 hours, so the text gives two different recovery times for the same result.
entries.snippet: recovering 24 h later, although at higher intensities

entries.proposition: Kainate result: knockout mice showed more hippocampal seizures and more after-discharges (21.4 versus 6.25 percent before, 64.2 versus 25 percent after kainate).
entries.snippet: 21.4% vs. 6.25% before, and 64.2% vs. 25% after kainate injection

entries.proposition: Sample sizes differ between text and legends (14 control and 10 knockout in the Results text; n = 8 and n = 12 controls in Figure 2 and 3 legends; n = 16 and 14 in Figure 5).
entries.snippet: An initial number of 14 Control and 10 GYS1Nestin-KO mice were used.

entries.proposition: Mechanistic statements are conjecture: possible roles of astrocytic potassium and glutamate uptake or of high-firing inhibitory neurons are offered, not tested; HIF is mentioned as a protective factor from other work.
entries.snippet: Alternatively, our results could be attributed to inhibitory neurons firing at very high frequency

entries.proposition: Direction of the conclusion: glycogen is protective in hypoxia and against seizures, on the basis of a loss-of-function allele only (no glycogen measurement, no rescue).
entries.snippet: Our results demonstrate the importance of brain glycogen in energetically challenging conditions.

entries.proposition: Figures 1 to 5 opened: Fig 1 power spectra at 760 and 405 mmHg and 24 h after (asterisk at 6-10 Hz at 15 and 60 min); Fig 2 and 3 input/output curves and paired-pulse ratios (differences abolished at 60 min, back at 24 h); Fig 4 kainate-evoked seizure traces; Fig 5 train-stimulation after-discharges with bar charts of seizure percentage before and after kainate.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 1 spectra bars WT versus KO; Figure 2 and 3 amplitude and St2/St1 plots at four time points; Figure 4 LFP traces and spectra before and after kainate; Figure 5 fEPSP traces and seizure percentage bars.
